newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam says president "tired", been told to rest.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam says president "tired", been told to rest.

text.p: Vietnamese President Le Duc Anh is feeling tired and has been told by doctors to rest, a foreign ministry spokesman said on Monday in response to inquiries about reports that the 75-year-old president had suffered a stroke.
"What we know is that President Le Duc Anh is tired and, as requested by doctors, he needs a rest," the spokesman said in a statement.

The spokesman said Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi would receive South Korea's President Kim Young-sam, whom Anh had invited for an official visit this week. He said vice-president Nguyen Thi Binh would also be present at the reception.

Political and diplomatic sources said Anh, a member of the communist country's leadership triumvirate, was paralysed down one side as a result of a stroke and doctors were not optimistic that he would recover sufficiently to carry on as president.
Under the constitution, when the country's president is incapacitated for work over "a long period of time" the vice-president must act in his place.

If the post falls vacant, the vice-president must stand in until the election of a new president by the National Assembly. The assembly's next session is not due until March or April, but an extraordinary session could be convened.
